OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows  operating system.
The ZED  CHOP  reads positional and plane tracking from the ZED camera. It can additionally use a UV to find plane in the room, and return information about that plane such as it's size/orientation either relative to the camera, or the room itself.
When the Camera Transform parameter is enabled, we provide the plane orientation data as well as the following.
Channel Name
Description
camera:tx ,  camera:ty ,  camera:tz
Camera translation vector
camera:rx ,  camera:ry ,  camera:rz
Camera rotation vector
When Body Tracking is enabled, the Body 3D parameter enables  tx tz tz  positions values for each joint (i.e.  p1/body/shoulder_l:tx  is the position x component of the left shoulder for the first tracked body), the Body 2D parameter
enables  u v  coordinates. The following are the supported body landmarks for 18, 34, and 38 joints listed
in the  ZED Body Tracking  documentation.
The ZED  CHOP  supports multiple body tracking with the Max Bodies parameter. Each of the previous as well as following channel names can be prepended with  p#  indicating which
body this pertains to, i.e. the  p3/body/neck:tx  channel indicates the neck position x component for the third tracked body.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When 'On' data is captured from the ZED camera.

parameters.label: ZED  TOP
parameters.name: zedtop
parameters.description: The name of the primary  ZED TOP  that is configuring the camera. The primary  TOP  controls which camera the  CHOP  receives data from.

parameters.label: Camera Transform
parameters.name: cameratransform
parameters.description: Enables transformation, which returns the position and rotation of the camera.

parameters.label: Camera Transform
parameters.name: resetcameratransform
parameters.description: Zeros out the current camera position, effectively makes the current position the new origin.

parameters.label: Plane Orientation
parameters.name: planeorientation
parameters.description: Enables plane at point, which returns the position of the plane corresponding the UV coordinate.

parameters.label: Get Plane
parameters.name: getplane
parameters.description: Returns the camera position relative to the initial position of the camera. A  tx ,  ty ,  tz  triplet of channels will be output for the position of the camera in meters. An  rx ,  ry ,  rz  triplet will be output for the orientation.

parameters.label: Pulse
parameters.name: getplanepulse
parameters.description: Instantly returns the camera position relative to the initial position of the camera.

parameters.label: Plane  Reference   Frame
parameters.name: planereferenceframe
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls if the panel coordinates will be given relative to the camera or the world.

parameters.label: World
parameters.name: world
parameters.description: Plane position outputs are relative to the initial position of the camera.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: Plane position outputs are relative to the previous position of the camera.

parameters.label: Plane Point U
parameters.name: planepointu
parameters.description: Sets the U coordinate of the point in the image to extract plane position.

parameters.label: Plane Point V
parameters.name: planepointv
parameters.description: Sets the V coordinate of the point in the image to extract plane position.

parameters.label: Plane Position
parameters.name: planeposition
parameters.description: Returns  tx ,  ty , and  tz  position channels of the center of the plane.

parameters.label: Plane Rotation
parameters.name: planerotation
parameters.description: Returns  rx ,  ry , and  rz  rotation channels for the plane.

parameters.label: Plane Normal
parameters.name: planenormal
parameters.description: Returns  nx ,  ny , and  nz  normal channels of the plane.

parameters.label: Plane Size
parameters.name: planesize
parameters.description: Returns size of the bounding rectangle of the plane.

parameters.label: Body Tracking
parameters.name: bodytracking
parameters.description: ⊞  - Body tracking allows for tracking human skeletons that are found in the video frame. Each mode uses an AI model that will need to be trained one for your  GPU . This will take several minutes, but only needs to be done once per model per machine, as long as the  GPU  isn't changed. For models where the 'Joint Mode' parameter is disabled, the outputs will be 'Absolute'.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Body Tracking is disabled.

parameters.label: Skeleton - 18 Joints
parameters.name: skeleton18
parameters.description: Tracks an 18 joint skeleton as described in  this article .

parameters.label: Skeleton - 34 Joints
parameters.name: skeleton34
parameters.description: Tracks an 34 joint skeleton as described in  this article . The positions and rotations are relative to the parent joints, as described in that article, where the 0 joint is the 'root' joint.

parameters.label: Max Bodies
parameters.name: maxbodies
parameters.description: The maximum number of bodies that will be tracked.

parameters.label: Body 3D
parameters.name: body3d
parameters.description: Enable to output 3D positions. Rotations will be included if the Joint Mode is set to 'Relative'.

parameters.label: Joint Mode
parameters.name: jointmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls if the joint values are given in absolute in scene or relative to each other.

parameters.label: Absolute Position
parameters.name: absolute
parameters.description: Absolute XYZ positions of each in space, given in meters.

parameters.label: Relative, with Orientation
parameters.name: relative
parameters.description: 3D skeleton positions and rotations in heriachical terms, each relative to a parent joint.

parameters.label: Body 2D
parameters.name: body2d
parameters.description: 2D normalized UV coordinates for each joint, giving their position within the image.

parameters.label: Aspect Correct UVs
parameters.name: aspectcorrectuv
parameters.description: Corrects the UV coordinate using the aspect ratio. For a 2x1 aspect ratio, a normalized coordinate of (0.25, 0.25) will cover a quarter of the width and an eighth of the height, not a quarter of the height. This mode is useful when performing orthographic rendering or using the Fraction Aspect unit within TOPs.

parameters.label: Bounding Boxes
parameters.name: boundingboxes
parameters.description: Enable bounding boxes. Head bounding box is only enabled when Body 3D is enabled.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
